metadata.dataset_name: Mumbai Locality Urban Safety & Infrastructure Vulnerability Index

benchmark.description: Comparative analysis: Naive unweighted per-capita crime rate compared against the formula-derived Composite Vulnerability Indicator. This score is an administrative demonstration indicator, not an empirical probability of criminal incidence.

models.name: Formula-Derived Composite Indicator
models.features_used: Total Crimes, Density, Police Density, UHI, Internet %

eda_findings.title: Chowki Load Strain in High-Density Corridors
eda_findings.headline: Top-quartile density corridors bear 2.0x higher incident load per police chowki (1.98x locality mean, 1.82x pooled aggregate).
eda_findings.takeaway: High-density transit and commercial corridors (e.g., Saki Naka, Mogra Village, Kurla) experience higher incident pressure per police outpost. In areas where population density exceeds 48,000/km², police chowkis bear roughly twice the incident load of low-density areas.

eda_findings.title: Built-Environment Density & Incident Association
eda_findings.headline: High-UHI built corridors exhibit 1.8x higher reported incidents, with a statistically significant moderate correlation (Spearman ρ = 0.36, p < 1e-15).
eda_findings.takeaway: Urban Heat Island index serves as an environmental proxy for dense, paved, built-up corridors with low vegetative cover. Localities in the highest UHI category average 12.2 recorded safety incidents compared to 6.7 in low-UHI zones (1.8x ratio; baseline indicator: crimes against women subset). This empirical correlation highlights the value of municipal lighting and streetscape design, but represents an environmental association rather than thermal causation.

eda_findings.title: Digital Connectivity & Vulnerability Indicator Disparity
eda_findings.headline: Lower internet penetration areas exhibit higher composite risk scores (14.0 vs 8.2, a +5.9 point disparity).
eda_findings.takeaway: Neighborhoods in the lowest digital penetration tier average a risk index of 14.0 compared to 8.2 in high-connectivity areas (a +5.9 point gap). While lower digital access correlates negatively with recorded total crimes (Spearman ρ = -0.30), the composite score accounts for infrastructure and crowd strain, counteracting reporting friction in underserved communities.
